topic_concept: Image Formation and Aperture of Convex Lens
question_text: A converging lens of focal length 25 cm projects an image of an illuminated slide. If the upper half of the lens is blocked by an opaque cover, describe the change in the projected image.

evidence_rationale: Believes covering half the lens cuts the image in half, misunderstanding that every point on the lens receives light from every point on the object.
diagram_description: Convex lens with lower half covered by black opaque cardboard. Object placed beyond 2F forms a complete real inverted image on the screen with reduced brightness.

topic_concept: Real Image Formation in Space
question_text: A student forms a sharp real image on a viewing card using a lens of f = 25 cm. When the card is taken away, what happens to the real image?
correct_answer_and_steps: The real inverted image still exists in empty space at that exact focal position (aerial image). The screen merely scatters light diffusely so observers can view it from all angles; the convergence of light rays occurs independently of the screen.

question_text: A person with myopia has a far point of 200 cm. What type of corrective spectacle lens is needed to restore normal distant vision?

question_text: In the dispersion of white light by a glass prism, which color of light travels fastest in glass and which deviates the least?
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.

misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed and Deviation Inversion
evidence_rationale: Believes red light is deflected most or that red travels slowest in glass, inverting the Cauchy dispersion relation.
diagram_description: Equilateral glass prism with white light incident. Red refracts least (top of band), Violet refracts most (bottom of band).

topic_concept: Scattering of Light and Colour of the Sky
question_text: What physical optical process is responsible for the blue color of the clear sky?
correct_answer_and_steps: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric gas molecules (N2, O2) whose size is smaller than visible wavelengths. The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.

question_text: Why does the clear daytime sky appear blue to an observer on Earth, but appears dark black to an astronaut in space without an atmosphere?
correct_answer_and_steps: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric gas molecules (N2, O2) whose size is smaller than visible wavelengths. The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (I ~ 1/lambda^4). Shorter blue wavelengths scatter roughly 16 times more strongly than red, illuminating the sky blue from all directions.

evidence_rationale: Believes the sky is blue because it reflects ocean water, or confuses wavelength dependence in Rayleigh scattering.
diagram_description: Sunlight striking atmospheric gas molecules. Blue light scatters in all directions (I ~ 1/lambda^4); red transmits through.

topic_concept: Parallel Circuits and Source Potential Difference
question_text: In a domestic parallel household circuit, what happens to the current through a room lamp when a powerful electric heater is switched ON in parallel?
correct_answer_and_steps: Brightness of B1 is UNCHANGED. The battery maintains a constant potential difference V across each parallel branch (V1 = V2 = V). Current in branch 1 remains I1 = V/R. Adding branch 2 lowers the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R/2), so the battery supplies TWICE the total current (I_total = 2I).
student_response: The battery delivers a constant total current of 2 A under all circumstances; connecting more appliances merely starves each appliance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source
evidence_rationale: Believes a battery produces a fixed constant total current regardless of what external resistance network is connected.

question_text: A student adds a second resistor of 4 ohms in parallel across an existing 4 ohm resistor. How does the total circuit resistance change?
correct_answer_and_steps: In parallel: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2, so R_eq = (R1 * R2) / (R1 + R2). Adding another resistor in parallel ALWAYS decreases equivalent resistance because it creates an additional pathway for charge to flow.
student_response: Connecting resistors together always increases the total circuit resistance, so parallel resistance is higher than either branch.
evidence_rationale: Overgeneralizes series addition to parallel circuits, believing adding resistors in parallel increases the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R1 + R2).

correct_answer_and_steps: Zero force. The magnetic force on a charged particle is given by the Lorentz force equation F = q * (v x B) = q * v * B * sin(theta). When the charge is stationary (velocity v = 0), the magnetic force is strictly zero. Magnetic poles are dipoles arising from moving charges/spins, not electrostatic monopoles.
student_response: North pole has positive static electricity and south pole has negative static electricity.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Equivalence Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Conflates magnetic poles with electrostatic charges, believing North poles are positively charged and attract stationary electrons.
diagram_description: Stationary electron placed near North pole of bar magnet. Magnetic force F = q(v x B) = 0 because v = 0.

correct_answer_and_steps: No two magnetic field lines can ever cross each other. topic_concept: Colour of the Sun at Sunrise and Sunset
question_text: What optical phenomenon causes the reddish appearance of the Sun near the horizon?
correct_answer_and_steps: Near the horizon, sunlight must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere. By Rayleigh scattering (I ~ 1/lambda^4), shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered away in all directions before reaching the observer. Only the longer, least-scattered red wavelengths penetrate the thick path directly into our eyes.
student_response: Sun appears red at sunset because red light is scattered the most by dust particles in the evening.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-005: Sunset Red Absorption / Temperature Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes the Sun appears reddish at sunset because the Sun physically cools down, or because red light is absorbed by clouds.
diagram_description: Sun near horizon traversing longer atmospheric path. Blue light is scattered away; least scattered red light reaches observer.

correct_answer_and_steps: Resistance is halved (R' = R/2) because R is directly proportional to length (R = rho * L / A). However, resistivity rho remains STRICTLY UNCHANGED. Resistivity is an intrinsic material property that depends only on the chemical nature of the substance and temperature, not on length, area, or shape.
student_response: if u double the length of a wire, both its resistance and its resistivity double.
evidence_rationale: Believes resistivity (rho) depends on the dimensions (length or area) of a wire, wrongly concluding that cutting a wire in half halves its resistivity.
diagram_description: Cylindrical copper wire of length L and cross-section A cut in half into length L/2. Resistance is halved (R/2); resistivity rho remains strictly identical.

question_text: In a circuit with a bulb glowing brightly, an ideal conducting wire (R = 0) is connected in parallel with the bulb. Does the bulb remain lit?

In parallel, current divides inversely proportional to resistance (I_bulb / I_wire = R_wire / R_bulb = 0). Practically 100% of the current flows through the bypass wire, short-circuiting the bulb so zero current flows through its filament.

correct_answer_and_steps: Mass on Moon = 60 kg (UNCHANGED). Weight on Moon = m * g_moon = 60 * 1.63 = 98 N (or 588 / 6 = 98 N). Weight is the gravitational force exerted on the object (W = mg), which varies with local gravity.

question_text: How does the gravitational force between two planets change if the distance between them is tripled?
correct_answer_and_steps: The new force is 25 N (one-fourth of the original force: F' = F / 4 = 100 / 4 = 25 N). Gravitation obeys the inverse-square law: F = G * M * m / r^2. Replacing r with 2r gives (2r)^2 = 4r^2 in the denominator, reducing the force by a factor of 4, NOT 2.

misconception_label: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Treats gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance (1/r) rather than distance squared (1/r^2), wrongly concluding that doubling distance cuts force in half.

correct_answer_and_steps: The new force is 25 N (one-fourth of the original force: F' = F / 4 = 100 / 4 = 25 N). Gravitation obeys the inverse-square law: F = G * M * m / r^2. Replacing r with 2r gives (2r)^2 = 4r^2 in the denominator, reducing the force by a factor of 4, NOT 2.

misconception_label: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Treats gravitational force as inversely proportional to distance (1/r) rather than distance squared (1/r^2), wrongly concluding that doubling distance cuts force in half.
diagram_description: Two masses separated by distance r (force F). When separation is increased to 2r, force drops to F/4.

topic_concept: Work Done by Centripetal / Gravitational Force in Circular Motion
question_text: Does the gravitational force of the Sun do work on the Earth as it moves in its approximately circular orbit?
correct_answer_and_steps: Work done is strictly 0 J. Gravitational force acts radially inward towards Earth's center, while the instantaneous displacement of the satellite is tangential along the circle. The angle between force and displacement is always 90 degrees. Since W = F * d * cos(90 deg) = 0, gravity does zero work on the satellite, keeping its kinetic energy constant.
